post.description:
Stripe webhook handler for credit pack purchases and retired subscription events.

Signature verification runs first for all requests. Non-pack event types
still return 410 Gone (the retirement contract for BetterAuth-owned events).

Pack path (checkout.session.completed / checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded):
- Validates the session metadata against the server-side catalog.
- Lazily opens an admin session inside the pack branch only (not for probes
  or retired events — no DB work for unrelated traffic).
- Issues an exactly-once ledger grant via pack_topup:{session_id} key.
- Permanent rejects (bad metadata, amount mismatch, org not found) return
  200 + error log so Stripe does not retry forever and auto-disable the endpoint.
- Transient DB faults bubble as 500 so Stripe retries (idempotency absorbs replay).

The webhook ALWAYS credits a paid pack regardless of CREDIT_PACKS_ENABLED —
a flag flip between purchase and delivery must never drop paid money.

get.description:
Human confirmation landing page ONLY — no state change, ever.

Corporate mail-security scanners/prefetchers (SafeLinks, Mimecast,
Barracuda) routinely GET every link in a delivered email, including
`List-Unsubscribe`. A mutating GET would silently unsubscribe opted-in
users on delivery, before a human ever sees the message. Token
verification here is a pure, DB-free HMAC check
(`resolve_unsubscribe_token`) purely to decide which page to render, and
which email kind to name on it.

post.description:
RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe. Handles BOTH triggers identically:
a mail client's automated `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-
Click` POST, and a human clicking the confirm button on the GET page's
form — RFC 8058 intentionally allows the provider to act on the POST
alone, no further confirmation step.

The token's purpose decides what is turned off, and only that:

* `digest:` sets `digest_opt_in = false` AND records an
  `email_suppression` entry, so ANY future digest send checks and skips
  this address, not just this user's own preference (belt-and-suspenders:
  covers a re-opt-in racing a stale queued send, and gives support a
  durable audit trail of consent withdrawal).
* `deadlines:` sets `deadline_reminders_opt_in = false` and NOTHING else.
  Suppression is address-wide, so writing one here would silently stop a
  user's digest, their briefcase mail and their invitations because they
  turned off one daily reminder. Turning off one email kind must mean
  exactly that (#4020 item 12).

delete.description:
Detach a member from the caller's active org. Does NOT touch the user row.

The user retains login, retains memberships in other orgs, and can be
re-added later via the invite flow. This is what "Remove member" in the
settings UI maps to.

The member's briefcases in THIS org are reassigned to the surviving
admin `pick_departure_inheritor` selects, before the membership row goes
(#2175 — the matter survives; an org admin inherits it). Since
`2026_09_02_briefcase_rls_repoint` (#2202 P2) briefcase RLS reads
`org_id` directly, so org visibility no longer depends on this
ordering — but reassignment must still precede removal because
ownership itself is `user_id`-keyed at the application layer
(`BriefcaseRepository.list_by_user`/`get`/`owned_ids` carry no RLS of
their own): a departed owner's briefcases would sit org-visible but
unowned by any live member's matter list until an admin reassigns them.
The removal is recorded in the org's audit log (`org.member_departed`).

Authorisation:
  - Caller must be admin or owner of the active org (caller.org_id).
  - Cannot remove the org owner — must transfer ownership first.
  - Cannot remove self — there is no "leave my own org" via this path.

For a full platform-wide soft-ban use BetterAuth's admin ban
(frontend/apps/nuxt/server/api/v1/admin/users/**) instead.

post.description:
Transfer ownership of the caller's active org to another member.

The ONE place 'owner' may be assigned: the invite path and the
strictly-below rank matrix (`_require_org_role_change_allowed`) both
refuse it by design, so this endpoint is what the "transfer ownership
first" errors in `remove_org_member` and the account-deletion sole-owner
block point at (#2203).

The caller (current owner) becomes 'admin' and the target becomes
'owner' in a single UPDATE inside the request transaction — never two
owners, never zero: an interruption or a raced transfer rolls the whole
request back with the old owner intact
(`OrgMembersRepository.transfer_ownership`).

Authorisation:
  - Caller must be the org owner. Not platform admins — ownership moves
    only by the owner's own explicit act.
  - Target must be a member of the active org, not 'external' (external
    counsel never owns the org), and not mid-deletion (#2134's
    `deletion_started_at` stamp — a vanishing owner is zero owners by
    another door).
  - Personal orgs (org id == caller id, the org-of-one convention) are
    refused: that org IS the person — and single-seat paid entitlement
    resolution fast-paths on `user_id == org_id`
    (`services/seat_resolution.py`), so transferring it would leave the
    ex-owner still resolving the paid profile.

Account deletion (#2134): a sole owner blocked by the 409 calls this,
then retries deletion — no longer an owner, they depart as an ordinary
member and the org survives under the new owner. Seats and Stripe are
untouched: seats are named per user, the subscription is org-keyed, and
billing management gates on the owner/admin role set which both parties
still satisfy.

get.description:
Elefant Credits balance + catalog; funds the lazy monthly grant before reading.

``enabled``/``packs_enabled`` mirror settings.app.credits_enforcement_enabled
and .credit_packs_enabled — this is the FE's render gate (see plan doc): a
global deployment flag, not a per-org plan entitlement, so it deliberately
does not live on /entitlements. Never 404s (unlike the pack-purchase
endpoint) so the FE can read `enabled: false` and render nothing.

Fund-on-read: when the enforcement flag is on (the same gate-1 condition
the gated-request path applies), the read runs the exact ensure_funded
funnel from dependencies.check_credits before computing ``balance``, so a
user's first balance read shows the period's grant instead of a stale
0-of-N. Enrollment semantics are unchanged: ensure_funded only writes a
grant for profiles with a MONTHLY_CREDIT_GRANTS entry; ungated profiles
and missing orgs return False with no enrolling write, so a read can only
enroll an org whose first gated request would have enrolled it anyway.
Concurrency-safe via the same server-generated idempotency key + partial
unique index (and the per-org advisory lock inside the expiry paths);
steady-state cost is ensure_funded's single index-only fast-path SELECT.
Best-effort: ensure_funded is internally fail-open (savepoint), and the
extra try/except here guarantees a funding fault can never 5xx this read —
it logs ``credits_fund_on_read_failed`` and serves the unfunded balance.

``monthly_grant``/``interval`` resolution mirrors ensure_funded's profile +
cadence lookup exactly (weekly checked first, monthly as fallback).
``session`` resolves to the same per-request session backing the repos
(FastAPI dependency caching), so the savepoint wraps the repo SQL.

get.description:
Public: live per-index and per-jurisdiction document counts for the country pages.

Reuses the backend's existing working ES adapter (get_es_adapter()) — the
FE previously queried Elasticsearch directly with its own NUXT_ELASTIC_API_KEY,
which went stale on every backend key rotation and silently zeroed every
jurisdiction's coverage stats. This is now the only ES credential path for
coverage. Cached for SEARCH_COVERAGE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS. No auth (registered
in settings.app.public_paths).

A degraded result is NOT cached, where "degraded" is scoped to the marketing
surface (is_degraded / _marketing_index_names) — a held-back region's own
index failing (CA today) does not count. Caching a genuinely degraded result
turns a transient search outage into an hour of published wrong answers, and
the frontend proxy caches on top of that — #2349 was served for up to two
hours from a single failed fetch. An uncached degraded response now costs one
registry-wide ES round trip per request until search recovers (#2384 collapsed
the per-index fan-out into the single query `registered_index_doc_counts` also
serves the empty-index canary from) — cheap, but not free, so a sustained
outage still adds load, and it is why a held-back region's failure must not
trigger it (#2377).

post.description: Send message (non-streaming). Returns immediately after saving.

Stream chat message response.

**Content negotiation:** Set `Accept: text/event-stream` for SSE format,
otherwise defaults to `application/x-ndjson`.

**Chunk lifecycle:**

| type       | value                  | description                    |
|------------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `status`   | status string          | Processing status updates      |
| `delta`    | partial text           | Incremental assistant response |
| `thinking` | partial thinking text  | Model reasoning tokens         |
| `done`     | `"completed"`          | Stream finished                |
| `error`    | `{code, message}`      | Structured failure (terminal)  |

Every successful stream ends with exactly one `done`. On failure the
terminal event is a structured `error` and `done` is NOT emitted.
`code` is one of the stable `StreamErrorCode` values; `message` is
user-safe (no exception repr or stack fragments).

post.description:
Share a briefcase with another user, by id or by email (#2397 Part 1).

Server-side gates, in the order they are asked:
  - external-sharing policy: when the sharee is NOT a member of the
    caller's active org, `organizations.sharing_policy` must be
    `external_allowed` (#1797). Every org defaults to `org_only`, which
    is the flat refusal this route has always emitted — only now an org
    admin can lift it. In-org shares never consult it: a governance
    switch must not be able to break a single internal share.
  - plan ceiling: `max_share_permission` caps the tier this org may
    grant. Pro/Explorer share at `view`; Business+ up to `full`; free,
    API and mammoth_staff cannot share at all and get the same
    `feature_disabled` 403 the retired `require_team_features` dep
    emitted (#1822).
  - external clamp: an external grant is silently clamped to `view`
    ahead of the ceiling check, no matter what tier the plan would
    otherwise allow (Q2, #1823, tracked by #2397). `full` is a write
    capability and the cross-org write-side guard for it doesn't exist
    yet.

Why the policy is asked FIRST, ahead of the ceiling: the two denials mean
different things and only one of them is actionable by the caller. "Your
org does not permit external sharing" is a governance answer an admin
clears; "your plan cannot share at this tier" is an upsell. A free-plan org
sharing externally is refused by both, and answering
`external_sharing_disabled` is the honest one — lifting the plan would not
make the grant legal. The FE keys its velvet rope off `reason`, so this
ordering is a contract, not a detail.

The membership lookup therefore moves ahead of the ceiling too: the policy
gate's precondition is "is this person a member?", so the answer has to be
in hand before either gate runs.

`BriefcaseShareRequest` is an OpenAPI-visible union: `sharee_id` OR
`sharee_email`, exactly one. An email is resolved against
`web."user"` directly (`get_identity_by_email` — RLS-independent, unlike
`UsersRepository.get_by_email`'s `org_members` join, which is scoped to
the CALLER's active org and would silently miss an existing user who
belongs to a different one, #2397 C3): a hit falls through the ordinary
`sharee_id` path below unchanged (in-org keeps `full`); a miss mints a
`briefcase_share_invitations` row instead of a `briefcase_shares` row —
there is no user id to share WITH yet.

Wave 5): legislation changes recorded in the alerts ledger since `since`,
or straight from `cursor` to page forward.

A thin read over `legislation_change` — Wave 2's hourly diff job is the
only writer; this never re-diffs ES/GCS and never mutates.

Entitlement gate: `require_full_seat` (this router's own dependency) only
excludes `mammoth_staff` seats — every other caller, paid or free, passed
with no check that the org actually bought this separately-sold API tier.
`ensure_legislation_changes_entitlement` closes that gap (403 for both a
service-principal API key and a logged-in human JWT); the MCP tool twin
(`ai/mcp_server.py`'s `list_legislation_changes`) calls the same function
so the two surfaces cannot diverge.

`cursor`, not `since`, pages forward. The diff job's whole tick writes
inside one transaction (see `services/legislation_alerts.run_diff`), and
Postgres `now()` is transaction-start time, so a batch of changes
routinely shares one identical `first_seen_at`. Feeding a bare
`first_seen_at` back as `since` would silently drop every row tied with
it past the first page's cut; `cursor` instead carries `(first_seen_at,
change_key)` and does an exact keyset comparison — see
`LegislationChangeRepository.since`'s docstring.

Session choice: `legislation_change` carries no RLS (org-agnostic corpus
data, granted a standing SELECT to the app role directly — see migration
`2026_07_16_legislation_alerts`), so this opens `tenant_session` as a
context manager rather than injecting `Depends(get_tenant_session)`. The
latter's `get_current_user` sub-dependency unconditionally 403s a
service-principal (org-bound API key, `user_id=None`) caller — exactly
the Tier-1 API-tier consumer this endpoint exists to serve (ADR-0003).
The RLS GUC `tenant_session` sets is an inert no-op against this
particular table (see `dependencies/repos.py`'s own rationale for
defensively setting it on non-RLS tables); using it anyway keeps every
DB-touching route in this codebase on the same session-opening idiom.

org's existing active one — see idempotency note below) and a
`webhook_subscriptions` row for `legal_request.completed`, so an

ChatMessageArtifact.title: ChatMessageArtifact
ChatMessageArtifact.description:
A durable artifact produced during a turn (#1544).

Today the only kind is a generated `document` — Ask Elf's draft tool
enqueues a job and the transcript keeps a reference so the card survives a
reload. Identifiers only: download URLs are fetched fresh from
`GET /documents/{id}` because job-result URLs are frozen at generation with
a 7-day TTL, so persisting one would guarantee a dead link.

`status` is the state at last write, not a live verdict: the entry lands
as `generating` the moment the job is enqueued (#1653 — a reload
mid-generation must render the pending card), and the terminal truth is
the client's job poll (`GET /jobs/{id}`), which flips the same card
ready/failed. Entries written before the field existed default to
`generating`, so a client must never treat it as proof the job is running.

LegalRequestMetricsResponse.title: LegalRequestMetricsResponse
LegalRequestMetricsResponse.description:
Org-level Mammoth impact metrics over a rolling window.

Counts-only aggregates, RLS-scoped to the caller's org (no PII). Throughput,
cycle time, `open_by_status`, and `closed_by_outcome` all cover the
trailing `window_days`. `open_by_status` and `closed_by_outcome` partition
the same created-in-window cohort by status: `closed_by_outcome` carries
the terminal statuses (completed/failed/cancelled), `open_by_status`
carries everything not yet terminal (pending/assigned/in_progress/
awaiting_review) — the two dicts always sum to `created`. `completed`
itself is a separate, narrower cohort: requests whose `completed_at` (not
`created_at`) falls in the window, so `completed` and
`closed_by_outcome['completed']` can legitimately differ.
`outstanding_awaiting_review_over_30d` is the one window-independent
figure: a standing count of `awaiting_review` requests — legitimate
pending work, never auto-failed — that have sat past the 30-day
needs-attention threshold.
`jurisdictions_delivered` lists the distinct human-readable jurisdiction
labels across completed-in-window requests (NULL/'unsure' excluded).

`distinct_handlers` / `colleagues_served` (distinct assignees / requestors
on the same completed rows) and `value` are ORG-OWNER-ONLY: in a small
team, per-handler counts are effectively named-colleague productivity data
(#995 owner decision). Non-owner viewers get null for all three —
enforced server-side, not by hiding them in the UI. `viewer_is_owner`
tells the client which it got.

``next_cursor``, when set, is an opaque ``"<first_seen_at ISO8601>|

``first_seen_at`` (the diff job writes a whole tick inside one
transaction, and Postgres ``now()`` is transaction-start time), so a
bare timestamp cursor would silently skip every row tied with the last
one returned. See ``LegislationChangeRepository.since``'s docstring.

then swept stale shows up under neither. Clients that want "what did I
decide this week" need a decision log, which does not exist.

MetalearnOrgMemberDigest.title: MetalearnOrgMemberDigest
MetalearnOrgMemberDigest.description:
One member's practice, as their org owner or admin may see it (#2001).

Deliberately NOT a subclass of ``MetalearnDigestResponse`` and deliberately
not built by trimming one. The owner drew a line through the digest on
2026-08-24, and a shared serialiser would put every future field on the
wrong side of it by default: this model carries the four things an
owner/admin may see and has no field for anything else, so widening the
self-view cannot widen this one.

What is missing is the point:

* **No learning conversations.** Neither their content nor how many there
  were. Reading a colleague's working notes is a different act from reading
  a summary of them, and nothing else in this product shows one person's
  chats to another. ``practice_topics`` — the areas they have been working
  in — is what the owner allowed instead.
* **No integrity verdicts.** Privacy invariant 5 would permit verdict kind
  and count; the owner excluded them anyway. That is a product choice about
  what an employer may see, NOT the invariant speaking, so a later reading
  of the invariant is not grounds to restore them.

`severity` are snapshots so the FE renders resolved findings without
fetching the prior result. `status` is model-assigned inference —
`unknown` is the honest degraded value when classification was
unavailable, never a guess. `matched_finding_key` names the CURRENT
round's finding a persisting concern maps to ("" when none does).

SearchCoverageResponse.title: SearchCoverageResponse
SearchCoverageResponse.description:
Live document counts for the country-page coverage stats.

``counts`` is per Elasticsearch index, keyed by the NORMALIZED base alias
name (normalize_index_name) — never a concrete ``_vN``/``_vNe5`` backing
name. Consumers (the FE's server-side jurisdiction aggregation) hold base
names, so a query-side reindex/repoint must not change these keys.
``jurisdictions`` is the same data pre-rolled up to jurisdiction level, so
a new consumer doesn't need to duplicate indices.py's mapping client-side.

A count is ``None`` when we could not obtain one (no search adapter, a
failed count query, a malformed ES reply) and an integer when we did —
including a genuine ``0``. The distinction is the whole point of the
field's nullability: before #2350 both collapsed to ``0``, and the public
marketing site rendered "we have nothing" whenever search was unreachable.
Never widen a ``None`` back to ``0`` to simplify a consumer.

language.description: ISO 639-1. Set means this entry is a language rendition of the provision (gh#2225); a reader partitions on it — set = rendition, None = version row.

translationStatus.title: Translationstatus
translationStatus.description: e.g. 'unofficial' — the original text remains the authority.

contentSha256.title: Contentsha256
contentSha256.description: sha256 of the version's text (gh#2716). Consecutive entries sharing one hash are one text re-emitted, not an amendment, and a reader collapses the run. None where the index maps no hash, and None never groups.

TimelineEntry.title: TimelineEntry
TimelineEntry.description: Single entry in a document's version timeline.

UnassignedDetail.title: UnassignedDetail
UnassignedDetail.description: Detail for an 'unassigned' action: assignee removed, request returns to pending.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction the user indicates for this request; 'unsure' when they cannot say.

UncertainInput.title: UncertainInput
UncertainInput.description:
Free-form input for an `uncertain` legal request.

The classifier agent reads `question_or_task` at execute time to
infer the concrete request_type.

UncertainResultPayload.title: UncertainResultPayload
UncertainResultPayload.description:
Result of an `uncertain` legal request (free-form intake the classifier
could not place; `notes` is the human sign-off path).

region.description: ISO country code selecting indices for that jurisdiction. US_* codes are state-level. Must match `legal_search.REGION_INDICES`.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Search mode. 'auto' detects from query; 'hybrid' = lexical ∪ semantic.

fuzzy.title: Fuzzy
fuzzy.description: Opt into fuzzy matching for the lexical query. Boolean and semantic modes are unchanged.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: search_after values from previous response for pagination.

rankingVariant.title: Rankingvariant
rankingVariant.description: Optional ranking experiment variant (e.g. 'experimental_a'). Logged for A/B analysis.

indiaSearchAll.title: Indiasearchall
indiaSearchAll.description: India 'Search all Indian judgments' toggle. False (default) queries the vectorised full-text judgments index; True switches the cases tier to the complete metadata catalog. Honoured only when region=IN and SEARCH_INDIA_ENABLED; legislation/regulatory selections are unaffected.

preferredLanguage.title: Preferredlanguage
preferredLanguage.description: ISO 639-1. Within a folded rendition group, front the member in this language. Never re-ranks or filters results.

asAtDate.title: Asatdate
asAtDate.description: Point-in-time cutoff: return the version of each provision in force on or before this date. Accepted only when every resolved index carries point-in-time versions (currently SG legislation and UK legislation provisions) — otherwise the request 422s. Not a filters field: index resolution (region/indexes) happens after `filters` parses, so this needs to validate after that resolution instead.

relaxed.title: Relaxed
relaxed.description: True when an empty boolean or keyword search was retried as hybrid.

degradedSources.title: Degradedsources
degradedSources.description: Search indices that did not answer, making this response incomplete.

queryTranslation.title: Querytranslation
queryTranslation.description: Corpus-language translation used by lexical search, when applicable.

UnknownNotification.title: UnknownNotification
UnknownNotification.description:
Fallback for notifications sent via /notifications/send with caller-supplied types.

The send and broadcast endpoints accept arbitrary type strings; this variant
absorbs them without validation of the metadata payload.

academicRole.title: Academicrole
academicRole.description: Professor/student standing on an academic plan. Null outside academic orgs and on any roster an org admin has not sorted yet.

fileId.title: Fileid
fileId.description: An uploaded file id from the presign flow; its text is saved.

academicRole.title: Academicrole
academicRole.description: Professor/student standing on an academic plan. Send an explicit null to clear it; omit the field to leave it unchanged.

WebhookDeliveryResponse.title: WebhookDeliveryResponse
WebhookDeliveryResponse.description:
One delivery attempt record, payload deliberately REDACTED (#1812 P1).

The stored payload carries the job's result (answer text) — the history
surface exposes event/status/attempt/timestamps only; the payload itself
reached the org's own receiver at delivery time.

StreamCitationSource.description:
A single citation captured during the turn.

Mirrors the dict shape `_record_turn_citations` (ai/functions.py) appends
to the turn-scoped capture list — same shape persisted to
`chat_message.sources`.
StreamCitationSource.title: StreamCitationSource

StreamCurrencyStatusEvent.description:
The turn's currency assessment status (#4288).

Mirrors `CurrencyAssessment.status` in services/currency_check.py. Emitted on
every assessed turn, so `unchecked` — the fail-open outcome, which carries no
verdicts — is a state the client can render instead of being byte-identical to
a turn that was checked and came back clean.
StreamCurrencyStatusEvent.title: StreamCurrencyStatusEvent

StreamDeliberationPromptValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamDeliberationPromptEvent.value.

Mirrors DeliberationPrompt in ai/streaming_events.py (issue #1550 P1).
`id` is the judgment_deliberations row the FE answers via POST
/chats/{chat_id}/deliberations/{id}. Elf's own position is stored on the
row, never streamed.
StreamDeliberationPromptValue.title: StreamDeliberationPromptValue

StreamDoctrineArtifact.description:
A curator-blessed doctrine chain recorded on the turn (#2536).

camelCase on the wire (`doctrineKey`), matching its REST twin
`ChatMessageDoctrineArtifact`.
StreamDoctrineArtifact.title: StreamDoctrineArtifact

StreamDoctrineBriefValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamDoctrineBriefEvent.value (#2536).

camelCase on the wire (`doctrineKey`) — mirrors `DoctrineBrief` in
ai/streaming_events.py, which dumps with `by_alias=True`.
StreamDoctrineBriefValue.title: StreamDoctrineBriefValue

StreamDocumentGeneratedValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamDocumentGeneratedEvent.value (#1544).

Mirrors DocumentGenerated in ai/streaming_events.py. Emitted mid-stream on
the chat surface when Ask Elf's `draft` tool enqueues a document job, so
the FE can render a generating->ready card. IDENTIFIERS AND TITLE ONLY —
never the draft's prose, and never a download URL (those are fetched fresh
from `GET /documents/{id}`; job-result URLs expire after 7 days).
StreamDocumentGeneratedValue.title: StreamDocumentGeneratedValue

StreamErrorValue.description:
Error payload nested under StreamErrorEvent.value.

Mirrors StreamError in ai/streaming_events.py.
StreamErrorValue.title: StreamErrorValue

StreamEscalationValue.description:
Escalation payload nested under StreamEscalationEvent.value.

Mirrors `Escalation` in ai/streaming_events.py (model-tiering P3 design §2
"UX"). `applied=True` is a real med->max model swap for this turn;
`applied=False` is the pin-suppression case — a non-blocking suggestion
only, since an explicit user model pick is never auto-escalated.

`"support"` (supported-answer guarantee) is the support gate's same-model
re-answer, not a tier swap — `from_tier == to_tier` for it.
StreamEscalationValue.title: StreamEscalationValue

StreamGraphArtifact.description:
A completed graph-analysis run recorded on the turn (#1967).

Mirrors the `chat_message.artifacts` jsonb entry for kind='graph_analysis'.
Seed legisIds only — the "open the coloured graph" affordance reads its
treatment colours from the shared edge_treatments cache the run warmed.
StreamGraphArtifact.title: StreamGraphArtifact

StreamGraphBriefValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamGraphBriefEvent.value (#1967).

Mirrors GraphBrief in ai/streaming_events.py. Emitted mid-stream when Ask
Elf's `graph_analysis` tool completes its treatment walk. Seed legisIds
only — never the brief's prose.
StreamGraphBriefValue.title: StreamGraphBriefValue

StreamHeartbeatEvent.description:
Keep-alive frame for long-running streams (PR-13 / BE.C68).

Receivers MUST accept and silently ignore. NOT a terminal event — the
stream still ends with a `done` or `error` frame after any heartbeats.
Added to prevent Cloud Run idle-proxy disconnects (~60s) from killing
long chat / orchestrate / search-summary sessions.
StreamHeartbeatEvent.title: StreamHeartbeatEvent

StreamMessageArtifact.description:
One durable artifact produced during the turn (#1544).

Mirrors the `chat_message.artifacts` jsonb entry the turn persister writes,
so a live client and a reloaded transcript render the same card from the
same shape. `kind` discriminates future artifact types (uploads, reviews);
`document` is the only one P1 emits. Identifiers only — download URLs are
fetched fresh from `GET /documents/{id}`, never frozen into the facet.
StreamMessageArtifact.title: StreamMessageArtifact

StreamMessageSavedValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamMessageSavedEvent.value.

Mirrors what the FE needs to attach feedback (thumbs up/down) to the
just-persisted assistant message without a follow-up GET. `sources`
carries the turn's citations inline so the FE can render them the moment
the answer finishes streaming, instead of only after a reload (#654
scope note — the live SSE frame previously carried only `message_id`).
`artifacts` does the same for document cards (#1544): the live frame and
the persisted row agree, so a reload changes nothing on screen.
StreamMessageSavedValue.title: StreamMessageSavedValue

StreamPhaseValue.description: Payload nested under StreamPhaseEvent.value. Mirrors TurnPhase.
StreamPhaseValue.title: StreamPhaseValue

StreamRetrievalStatusEvent.description: A retrieval limitation the reader needs beside the answer (#4392).
StreamRetrievalStatusEvent.title: StreamRetrievalStatusEvent

StreamRiskAlertValue.description:
Risk-advisory payload nested under StreamRiskAlertEvent.value.

Mirrors RiskAlert in ai/streaming_events.py. Emitted mid-stream on the chat
surface when legal-risk triage lands a RED/AMBER verdict. `tier` is the
effective (person-modulated) tier; `ack_required` is True for RED (FE blocks
on an interstitial), False for AMBER (passive banner).
StreamRiskAlertValue.title: StreamRiskAlertValue

StreamToolCallStartedValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamToolCallStartedEvent.value.

Mirrors ToolCallStarted in ai/streaming_events.py. Emitted the moment the
model invokes a tool (chat-stream rework Phase 1, 2026-07-13 design doc
§4.2) — `label` is the resolved, user-facing copy (e.g. "Searching
Elefant's legal corpus"), never the raw Python tool name.
StreamToolCallStartedValue.title: StreamToolCallStartedValue

StreamToolProgressValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamToolProgressEvent.value.

Mirrors ToolProgress in ai/streaming_events.py. Sub-step progress inside
an opaque, long-running tool call — today only the `research` tool's
Plan/Search/Curate/Analyse/Write graph, surfaced because that tool call
is otherwise invisible to the model runtime's own event stream for its
whole (up to 240s) duration.
StreamToolProgressValue.title: StreamToolProgressValue

StreamToolResultSource.description: One source returned by a retrieval tool for the grounding ledger.
StreamToolResultSource.title: StreamToolResultSource

StreamToolResultValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamToolResultEvent.value.

Mirrors ToolResult in ai/streaming_events.py. `sources_found` is
best-effort — most tools return prose today, not a structured list — so
it is commonly absent.
StreamToolResultValue.title: StreamToolResultValue

StreamTurnStartedValue.description:
Payload nested under StreamTurnStartedEvent.value.

Mirrors TurnStarted in ai/streaming_events.py (#1224 P2a). `turn_id` is
the durable chat_turn row created before the first token — the handle a
reconnecting client matches against the chat detail's `active_turn`.
StreamTurnStartedValue.title: StreamTurnStartedValue
